newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross to market Bristol-Myers' AIDS drug.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross to market Bristol-Myers' AIDS drug.

text.p: Osaka-based drug maker Green Cross Corp said on Wednesday will market Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's HIV drug in Japan.
It said it may start selling the drug in Japan by the end of July.

Bristol-Myers Squibb KK, the U.S. drug firm's Japanese unit, said in a statement that the drug, Zerit, was first introduced in the United States in 1994 and was currently undergoing an import approval review by the Japanese government.
Green Cross has been at the centre of a scandal surrounding blood products tainted with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.
Former Green Cross executives were indicted last October on charges of professional negligence for selling blood products that could infect patients with HIV.
